newsitem.title: UK: Copper, aluminium boosted by strong fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Copper, aluminium boosted by strong fundamentals.

text.p: Falling stocks of copper and rising U.S.offtake of aluminium drew the attention of both the industrial and speculator fraternity to the London Metal Exchange on Thursday.
In other markets cocoa dropped to a seven month low, sugar steadied after a lower production estimate from the Ukraine and silver turned lower.

Copper prices came within a whisker of breaking above a key barrier at $2,000 on Thursday on the London Metal Exchange (LME), but met tough resistance near that level, while aluminium finished up $19 and above previous resistance at $1,420.
"For the moment the short-term fundamentals which we can see are obviously supportive of higher prices," Angus MacMillan, analyst at Billiton Metals said.
"Selling above the market will cap any rally....but sellers may back off a bit while this strength continues," he added.
Benchmark three month copper futures finished the afternoon kerb at $1,993 a tonne, up $17 from Wednesday's afternoon close.

LME floor traders said prices rose in anticipation of another sizeable drawdown in LME copper stocks on Friday. Stocks have fallen over 115,000 tonnes in less than two months and are not far above the low point of 141,100 reached in July 1995.
It was being shipped to end-users in Europe and the Middle East as well as to China, traders said.
Although stocks were low and expected to fall further, doubts remained over the market's upside potential as producers appeared keen to sell into any rise.
Aluminium traders were encouraged by U.S. Aluminium Association data showing demand in the world's biggest market up by 8.5 percent in August from the previous month.
Analysts were also citing trade talk of the possibility of a meeting of leading producers in Moscow, to discuss the current statistical situation of the market, as potentially bullish.
London cocoa futures fell to their lowest since March this year as speculators became disillusioned with the market's sluggish performance of late and industry buyers withdrew.
March futures breached a previous support level at 975 sterling a tonne, which could signal further near term losses, and closed at 972 sterling, fown 17 from Wednesday.
A drop in Ukraine's expecations for its 1996/97 sugar output to 2.8 million tonnes from 3.2 million previously helped steady a previous lacklustre sugar market.
On the London bullion market silver lost most of the week's gains to close with the spot price around $4.90 an ounce after players became unnerved by a bout of fund selling in New York.
